findings: The ceiling is taken of the actual real left-degree lower bound. Integrality of host degree discharges ceil(F)<=degree. k>=32 and d>=k^3 pay the rounding loss and imply k<=D, d/2<=D<=d.

The actual bipartite branch width floor(k/4)+1 is retained, rather than uniformly overcharging it as k. Its guaranteed density gain is at least width*(1-16/k). The general branch uses actual width k and weakens its proved gain k-7 to k-16.

The selected-scale adapter maps witnesses and branch sets into the original graph. A too-dense selected induced core supplies a singleton-branch minor; otherwise d<k*d0 pays the witness-size normalization. No density discrepancy is assumed away.

BalancedDensityEscalation constructs an actual finite sequence by induction. Its actual branch-width product W is composed through genuine MinorModel.comp; the density scale is alpha^j*W*d. Both permissible widths make this scale grow by at least two each step.
Clique-minor exclusion transfers to every actual minor stage, so the previously proved finite logarithmic clique-density cap forces witness termination at the explicit numerical horizon.

The Bernoulli estimate with 32t<=k and j<t gives alpha^j>=1/2. The original-host pullback uses actual branch unions and target-edge injection, with |T|<=W|S| and E(target[S])<=E(G[T]). This pays the width product while retaining only a factor-two density loss.

The resulting witness simultaneously satisfies d|T|<=1600000*k^7*C^2 and d|T|<=1600000*k^7*E(G[T]), with a positive actual induced edge count. Its construction is internal, rather than an arithmetic witness premise.

The horizon t=Nat.log 2 C+1 and k=32(t+1) are chosen internally. The earlier elementary clique-density construction supplies C=24576*h*(Nat.log 2 h+2); the new numerical bound gives a literal degree-nine polylogarithmic loss.

The low-density case chooses an actual edge of the original graph from d>0 and positive host order, yielding a two-vertex induced witness. This removes the k^3 density prerequisite from the final positive-density witness theorem.

The high-girth join applies genuine induced-subgraph cycle inheritance and the established graph-level Moore bound to the constructed witness. Witness positivity supplies positive order for division/root extraction, closing the prior conditional density algebra.

The final sparsity theorem applies to the actual ordered greedy output and combines its established weighted spanner property, actual minor-freeness and actual girth. It has no supplied density witness, cleaning object, minor sequence, hierarchy or Moore certificate.

Edgeless and empty hosts are handled before forming edge/order density. The multiplicative coefficient fullDensityLoss(h) is separately bounded by an explicit constant times (Nat.log 2 h+2)^9, independent of the girth/stretch parameter.
final_domain: Finite simple undirected graph G; integer r>=1 and h>0; actual clique-minor exclusion; real weights strictly positive on every Sym2 value, as required by the existing greedy interface.
final_conclusion: The actual greedy output is a (2r-1)-spanner and has at most 2*fullDensityLoss(h)*h^(2/(r+1))*|V| edges. fullDensityLoss has the proved uniform degree-nine polylogarithmic bound.
